rule.from: the operator, 2026-11-24: "at the core stands the database schema ... after we design the schema we lock it in so the coding agents have to fall into compliance"
rule.text: The schema folders (schema/cortex, schema/ui, engines/<engine>/schema, features/<feature>/schema) are the database. Code reads and writes the tables they declare, with the columns they declare, and nothing else; no code creates, alters or drops a table, a column, an index or a constraint but the store, which does it from these files alone, and no code works out at run time what a file declares. A table, a column or a value the schema has no place for is a stop, not a workaround.
rule.breach: the store, which creates a database only from the schema folders and refuses a database whose tables, comments or rules differ from them; the spec check over the schema folders; review

rule.from: the operator, 2026-11-24: "its both referential integrity and data consistency preventing drift"
rule.text: Every reference between rows is a foreign key, every value is constrained by its type and its checks, and every rule a foreign key cannot state is a rule view of its owner's rules folder (broken_<rule>, the rows breaking it), which cortex.enforce_rules turns into deferred constraint triggers: the database itself refuses any commit that breaks one, whatever code or tool wrote it. Nothing is checked by convention alone, and no code turns a check off, disables a trigger or sets session_replication_role.
rule.breach: the store's tests, which plant a row breaking a foreign key and a check, and, for every rule view of every rules folder, the row its fixtures name, and prove each commit is refused; review

rule.from: the operator, 2026-11-24: "a cortex schema global and schema per engine"; docs/engines.xml
rule.text: What every engine shares is the cortex's; what is one engine's alone is that engine's, in its own tables in its own crate, in its own namespace engine_<engine> (engine_mysql.tables). Shared code (the model, the interface, the store, the server, the canvas) never names an engine, an engine table or an engine column; an engine never writes a cortex table's rows but through the interface, and never another engine's.
rule.breach: the architecture check (a database named outside its engine, an engine's table among them since each is named by its engine; and, from t03, every engine's field keys, kind ids, option keys, table and column names in shared code); the spec check (an engine table outside its engine's folder, or outside its engine's namespace); the kit

rule.from: the operator, 2026-11-24: "whatever schema we design it has to be versioned and extendable to accommodate new features"
rule.text: The schema grows by versions, never by rewrites. A new feature is a new owner with its own namespace, folder, versions and rules, and never changes the cortex's tables; a change to a table adds, and a rename or removal takes two versions, the data moved in the first. No version is ever edited once shipped: its checksum refuses it.
rule.breach: the store, which refuses a shipped version whose checksum changed and a database newer than its build; the upgrade test of every release from every earlier version; the spec check (a migration that drops or renames in the version that adds); review

rule.from: the operator, 2026-11-24: "never hardcode anything, store as params in the database"; "the more params the easier the mods, key value will do in the database"
rule.text: A value a person may want changed (a name, a label, a limit, a default, a link) is a row of cortex.workspace_parameters, read at run time; code holds only the key. A new value ships as a seed of a new version, inserted where its key is missing and never over a changed one.
rule.breach: the architecture check, from the store task, refusing the product's name written in code; the conformance kit's round trip under a renamed product; review

rule.from: docs/engines.xml; the MySQL engine as merged
rule.text: A schema written into the store and read back is the same schema: every part, every value, every order. What the model does not describe is kept exactly as written and written back in its place. Nothing is dropped, truncated, defaulted or summarised on the way in or out.
rule.breach: the kit's round trip of every sample through an engine's tables; the store's round trip of every sample of every engine

rule.text: The log (branches, turns, operations, row_changes, savepoints, versions) is appended to and never updated or deleted, but a turn's state and its verdict and a branch's newest turn; a change to the design is written in the same transaction as the operation that records it, with every row it changed, before and after.

rule.from: the operator, 2026-11-23: "this is not acceptable and create a harness to stop you"
rule.text: Shared code shows what an engine declares and never assumes one: no engine's connection field, kind, option, table or column is named in it. Every test of shared code runs on every engine of the registry, and the kit checks the interface on its own made-up example engine (crates/engine/tests/example); what each engine is tested on is data.
rule.breach: the architecture check's vocabulary guard (built by t03): every engine's field keys, kind ids, option keys, table and column names, read from what each declares, refused in shared code; the tests of shared code, run on every engine

rule.text: One session, one agent, sequential: the agent that holds a task does every step itself. It never spawns, delegates to or messages another agent, subagent or session, and never asks another model to build or verify a part.
rule.breach: the operator's build configuration (root method session), which denies the tools that spawn or message another agent; review of the PR's history

rule.from: the operator, 2026-11-24: "standards once abandoned it is impossible to troubleshoot; one fix will break 10 others"
rule.text: A task file lists under agent-decides the only things its agent decides: the names and the decomposition of private code inside the files it owns, the standard means of a step, the contents of its fixtures within the cases listed, its commit granularity. Everything else is written in the task file, the root, these rules, the schema folders or the merged code; a build that decides anything else is closed, and the step it departed from is named in the review.
rule.breach: review of the PR against the task file

rule.text: No commit, branch, PR, file or comment carries an attribution to a coding agent or a model: no co-author line, no generated-by line, no trailer. The work is the project's: its commits are pushed under the GitHub account of whoever runs the build (decision service-accounts), reviewed and merged by the operator.
rule.breach: the operator's build configuration (root method session), attribution off; review

rule.text: tools/check.sh is the one command every change passes, the same locally and in CI: formatting, lint, every test (the kit, the architecture check and the spec check among them). Nothing is done until it passes; its last line is in the PR.
rule.breach: CI; the gates of every task

rule.text: A build starts when a model is pointed at one task file, specs/tasks/<file>.xml, in any session the operator chooses (a new one, one that holds other work, or another agent's) on a checkout of the head of main updated from origin. Before it writes anything it reads, whole and in the order the root's method read gives, the files that order names, and from then on it works from them alone: nothing said earlier in the session, and nothing remembered from other work, is authority, and what the files do not say is a stop. In the database it acts only through the database's service accounts, sf_owner, sf_service and sf_reader (decision service-accounts). The task file's start element names the branch, the PR title and the read order; the agent writes its own label.
rule.breach: the PR body's statement of the session it ran in, the order the files were read and the account it acted as; review of the branch name, the PR title and every claim the PR makes against the files

rule.text: Every rule here binds every task, whether or not a gate of the task names it.
